samples.notes: Age and sex fields describe the whole sample, which is entirely kratom users. Every respondent is male (99 Malay, 1 Chinese); women refused to take part. Every respondent is a daily user, so no sex or frequency subgroups are extracted. The authors call every respondent 'people with kratom dependence' because of the daily-use inclusion rule, not because of the KDS result. People with significant health problems (kidney disease, diabetes, hypertension) were excluded. All respondents were employed. pct_other_opioid_use = 0 rests only on the urine rapid test (morphine MOP 0, methadone MTD 0). Self-reported opioid use was not collected, and the authors say some respondents used kratom to abstain from opioids. The main aim was urinary mitragynine by LC/MS/MS. No withdrawal scale was used.

samples.notes: Calculation: response 395/1152 = 34.3%. R1425 (EMA paper) covers the same 395 enrolled; 357 finished the EMA. Age, sex and n describe all 395 enrolled kratom users (all are users). Recruitment: mostly Reddit (36.7%) and Facebook (22.3%); the text does not say whether these were kratom-specific forums. About 26% came through the American Kratom Association, vendors, local advocacy groups or kratom stores, so the channel code needs a reviewer check. 36.7% were in alcohol or drug recovery; 28% of EMA completers used kratom as a long-term opioid substitute. Current non-prescribed opioid use or OUD not reported. Supplement (full survey; Supplemental Table 1 with KUD counts and other SUDs) not received. Withdrawal measured with SOWS (mean 13.5, SD 11.9) is context only.

codes.consistency_notes: 1) KUD prevalence: R1402 gives past-year KUD (>=2) 46.6% and lifetime 63.5% (n=395 implied). R1425 gives 238/357 (66.7%) meeting KUD (>=2) among EMA completers and says the survey covered 'past-year criteria'. That figure is closer to R1402's lifetime figure. R1402 values used, per the job. 2) R1402 abstract: 'KUD symptom counts were mostly in the mild/moderate range (80.7%)'. This does not match the text: of lifetime KUD cases, mild+moderate is 52.9/63.5 = 83.3%; of past-year cases it is 40.0/46.6 = 85.8%. 3) Demographics: R1402 says 81.3% White and 61.3% full-time employed; the R1425 table for the same 395 says White 359 (90.9%) and full-time 223 (56.5%). Age (38.1, SD 11.2) and male share (54.9%, 217/395) agree. 4) Dates: R1402 says enrolled July-November 2022; R1425 says recruited July 1-October 31, 2022. 5) Counts are derived from percentages; derived subcategories sum to the derived totals (131+78+42=251; 108+50+26=184).

codes.consistency_notes: 1) Denominators: Tables 4 and 5 use n=208 (lifetime leaf users, Table 3), even though Table 4 is titled 'past 3 months' and Table 5 'past 12 months'. Only 133 used leaves in the past 3 months, so people with no recent use are counted in the denominator. 2) SUDST labels: the Methods call the bands 'low / moderate / high level', while Table 5 calls them 'Mild / Moderate / Severe'. 3) The abstract prints '27.3' without a % sign. 4) Every figure checks against the table counts: SUDST leaves 137+46+23+2=208; any SUD 71/208=34.1%; cocktail 104+26+11+2=143; any SUD 39/143=27.3%; ASSIST leaves 100+101+7=208; cocktail 77+61+5=143. The only discrepancy is cocktail low risk: 77/143=53.8%, printed as 53.9%. 5) The text and abstract match the tables.
codes.note: Reference period for the denominator: LIFETIME use of kratom leaves (n=208). The authors' main estimate is past-12-month SUD (SUDST >=2) at 34.1% (71/208). The ASSIST time frame is the past 3 months, which has no exact code, so it is coded 'current'. Sex is not reported (the sample is presumably all male); age is for all 400 conscripts.
